audience.notes: Write for Mia and James (Sydney, 60 to 100 guests, planning 12 to 18 months out, jobs to keep running) and for Margaret, who is paying, reads every line, and is forwarding the link to her husband. Every section should give the couple something to picture and the parent something to trust. The bargain hunter should finish the piece knowing this is a planned, fee-based, From AUD 35,000+ service and not a discount route; never use 'cheap', 'budget', 'deal' or 'affordable' framing.

payload.search_intent: Commercial investigation. Searchers want to know whether they need a planner for a Tuscany wedding, who that should be when they live in Australia, and what it will cost and involve. Ranking pages answer with Italy-based planner homepages or Facebook threads; nobody answers from the Australian side.
payload.angle: The Australian-side guide the SERP is missing: what a Tuscany villa wedding planned from Sydney or Melbourne actually involves, in order, and which parts one Wedded Advisor handles from Australia (your time zone, AUD quotes and payments, legal recognition back home, long-haul guest travel, room blocks, older guests, wet-weather and villa rules) alongside the team on the ground in Tuscany.
serp_gaps_to_win: Planning from Australia in practice: time zone, who decides what and when, who is on the ground in Tuscany. No top-3 page in Sydney or Melbourne covers it beyond one-line tips.

Cost honesty in AUD: what drives the total for a villa wedding and how money is handled (fee agreed in writing, suppliers at standardised rates, AUD quotes). Cost is the most repeated PAA and related-search theme in every market, and no top-3 page gives a figure or an explanation.

Legal recognition for Australian passports, with official sources: civil ceremony in Italy versus legal at home plus a symbolic ceremony in Tuscany. Ranking pages either say 'it is easy' or name the Nulla Osta with no source.
Guest logistics from Australia: long-haul routing into Florence or Pisa, transfers to a rural villa, room blocks, and older guests (stairs, gravel, heat). Absent from every ranking page.
Wet weather, heat and villa rules (garden ceremony Plan B, music curfews, exclusive use). Only raised as unanswered questions or buried in testimonials.
A fair 'how to choose a planner' section that answers the Facebook threads ('do we need a planner', 'who is reasonably priced') without naming or linking any competitor.

outline.h2: Is a Tuscany villa right for your guest list?
outline.answers: Whether an exclusive-use villa suits a 60 to 100 guest wedding from Australia, and the honest trade-offs.
must_include: What 'villa wedding' means in practice: guests sleeping on site or nearby, multi-day use, welcome dinner and farewell lunch in the same place
Best months named by month (e.g. May, June, September, October) and an honest note on July and August heat, with temperatures in °C from an official source
Distance and transfer time from the nearest airports in km and minutes (researcher to source)
One concrete image for the couple: a long table dinner on the terrace at dusk
Soft link to /packages/italy/tuscany as the place to see villas we work with

outline.h2: Planning from Australia: your time zone, one person, and a team on the ground
outline.answers: How a wedding 16,000 km away gets planned without the couple losing sleep or their jobs (couple fear 1, parent fear 4).
must_include: The 5-step process by its exact names: Tell us anything; Meet your Wedded Advisor, and agree the fee; See real options, and choose; We contract and hold; You show up
One Wedded Advisor working in your time zone by phone, video or chat; reply within one business day
Who is physically present in Tuscany on the day: [[NEEDS: planning team to confirm the on-the-ground coordinator model]]
A realistic timeline from first call to wedding, e.g. 12 to 18 months [[NEEDS: planning team typical lead time]]
Whether a site visit is needed and what can be done on video

outline.h2: Marrying legally: civil ceremony in Italy or legal at home first
outline.answers: Whether the marriage will be valid in Australia, and which route suits which couple (parent fear 2).
must_include: The two routes explained plainly: a civil ceremony at an Italian town hall with Australian documents (Nulla Osta, apostille, translation) versus marrying legally in Australia and holding a symbolic ceremony at the villa
Terms explained on first use: Nulla Osta, apostille, symbolic ceremony
Official sources only, checked within 12 months: Italian consulate in Sydney (conssydney.esteri.it) or embassy in Canberra (ambcanberra.esteri.it), smartraveller.gov.au or dfat.gov.au
Close the section with: your Wedded Advisor confirms the current process for your passports
Short note that other passports differ (relevant to readers in other markets), without listing them

outline.h2: What a Tuscany villa wedding costs, in AUD
outline.answers: Roughly what to expect, what drives the number, and how the money is handled (parent fear 1, couple fear 4).
must_include: Price shown only as 'From AUD X' with the note that your Wedded Advisor confirms the real cost on your dates: [[NEEDS: Nic-approved From AUD figure for a Tuscany villa package]]
The main cost drivers: guest count, number of events, exclusive-use nights, season, catering style, transfers
How money is handled: planning fee agreed in writing before any work begins; suppliers paid at standardised industry rates, never a marked-up quote; quotes and payments in AUD
No price tables of 'cheap' options; no 'under $X' framing
Soft CTA line: 'Every price we quote is in AUD, so there is no currency surprise.'

outline.h2: Getting 80 guests from Sydney and Melbourne to the villa
outline.answers: How guests actually get there and where they stay, including grandparents (couple fear 3, parent fear 3).
must_include: Long-haul routing in general terms (one-stop via a hub into Florence or Pisa, or rail from Rome), airport names from official airport sites; no airline promises
Transfers from airport to villa: coaches and shuttles, timings, who meets guests
Room blocks explained on first use, and Wedded Privileges on every room guests book (benefits vary by property; conditions apply); link /privileges
Older and less mobile guests: ground-floor rooms, gravel paths, stairs, shade, shuttle between villa and ceremony spot
A guest information pack: what it contains and when it goes out

outline.h2: The work you will not see: rain, heat, curfews and the day itself
outline.answers: What happens behind the scenes so the day runs, shown as specifics rather than adjectives.
must_include: Wet-weather plan for a garden ceremony: indoor space or marquee held in advance, decision time on the day, who makes the call
Heat plan for summer dates: ceremony timing, shade, water stations

Villa rules many couples learn late: music curfews, noise limits, supplier restrictions or exclusivity, set-up and pack-down times [[NEEDS: researcher to confirm typical rules with an official or venue source]]
Run-of-day sheet and supplier briefings handled by your Wedded Advisor and the on-site team
No guarantees about weather, availability or approvals

outline.h2: Choosing a planner: what to ask before you sign
outline.answers: Do we need a planner, and how to judge any planner, Italy-based or Australia-based (answers the Facebook-thread question directly).
must_include: Fair framing: Italy-based planners know the ground; what an Australian-side Advisor adds is your time zone, AUD, home legal advice and guest travel from Australia

A short checklist of questions to ask any planner: how is the fee set and is it in writing; are supplier prices marked up; who attends the day; how many weddings do they run that week; what currency are quotes and payments in
No competitor names, no links to planners, directories or Facebook groups
Natural mention of Wedded Concierge and link to /concierge
